title: queue-only failure ×2 in one day: sql-driver-datetime-mysql-storage.test.ts "os migrate plan lists the MySQL widening (#3954)" — root-cause flake vs #9274 probe interference
body:
Filed by the PM seat closing out #9283's "Secondary, and separable" section, which is otherwise unowned. The gate side of #9283 is resolved (required-checks settings corrected by the maintainer); this card is the **failing test itself**, which has now failed on two independent merge-group builds in one day while staying green on every PR-side run:

| occurrence | where | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 10:10:24Z | `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-9270-…`, CI run [32017635668](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/32017635668) | red, **merged anyway** through the then-open required-checks hole (#9283) — so `main` briefly carried a commit whose full-suite run was red |
| ~12:53Z | `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-9290-862eb14…` (12:48Z batch) | red, PR #9290 correctly dequeued — that PR is `clean` and **waiting on this card** before anyone re-queues it |

Failing test, both times:

```
FAIL src/sql-driver-datetime-mysql-storage.test.ts
  > os migrate plan lists the MySQL widening (#3954)
```

## Why "re-queue and hope" is not the move

The test body runs and fails — this is not the runner-death class that a bare re-run legitimately answers. Two queue-side failures with consistent PR-side greens is a pattern with information in it; burning it with a blind re-queue wastes the only reproduction context we have.

## Hypotheses to test (from #9283, neither yet measured)

1. **Interference from #9274** (`sql-driver-diagnostic-value-probe.test.ts`, merged 09:55Z — *before both failures*): it creates tables (`probe_9160_mysql`) and deliberately raises errors against the **same live MySQL service** in the same suite run. Evidence against: #9274's own PR-side Temporal Conformance was green, and PR-side runs after it merged (e.g. #9290's head, base at 11:03Z+) are green too — so if this is it, it is order- or timing-dependent, which is exactly what a queue runner's different load profile could expose.
2. **Genuine flake against live MySQL 8.0** (timing/lock/init sensitivity in the widening-plan path). The merge-queue-triage bot reported one additional queue failure in the prior 24h — a possible third data point worth pulling.

## The work

- Reproduce against a live MySQL 8.0 (the repo's Temporal Conformance service recipe: `mysql:8.0`, `time_zone='+08:00'`, TZ=America/New_York process zone, `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`). Try: full `driver-sql` suite repeatedly; then the two files together in both orders; then parallel-worker configurations. The goal is a **measured reproduction or a measured exclusion**, not a guess.
- If interference: fix isolation (distinct schema/database per test file, or teardown discipline in the probe file) — ⛔ without weakening what either test asserts.
- If flake in the test: fix the race in the test's own setup/assertions — ⛔ never skip, quarantine, or retry-wrap it.
- If a real driver bug (order-dependent widening plan): that is the jackpot; fix the driver.
- Pull the logs of both failing runs first (links above) — the actual assertion diff may already discriminate between hypotheses.

## Unblocks

PR #9290 (re-queue once this is understood) · the queue's trust in `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, which is now in the required set — a flaky required check dequeues green PRs, which is expensive queue-wide.

Related: #9283 (both incidents' record) · #9274 (hypothesis 1) · #3954 (the test's origin) · #3942/#3979 (the temporal axis).
